est.how_body: Every mains-fail event is a battery test. If the battery ran out (LOW BATT / NE DOWN) we observe the true backup time. If PLN came back first (68% of events) we only know the battery lasted at least that long — a censored observation. Plain medians of the exhausted events are therefore biased low (in the test below: {bias} min). PBA uses Kaplan-Meier, which uses both kinds of observation: per site when it has its own events (ACTUAL), and comparable-site curves (class × battery type × NOP) for sites without measurement (ESTIMATED, floored at what the site already survived).
est.km.sub: Share of batteries still supplying the site after t minutes of PLN outage. Median = where the curve crosses 50%. Portfolio — not affected by the filter.
est.km.title: 3 · Battery survival curves (Kaplan-Meier)
est.test.expl: "Own-site history" is the best predictor (a site's own past events) — that is why measured sites use their own Kaplan-Meier value. For sites with no measurement, comparable-site KM is used: nearly unbiased, and it beats both the naive median and the gradient-boosting (AI) model. Each estimate shows a range of ± {mae} min and a confidence (Medium-Low if the site already survived an outage, else Low).
est.test.sub: Learn from Jan–Apr events of 70% of sites; predict the May–Jun BBT of the other 30% (sites the model never saw).
est.test.title: 2 · Estimation algorithm — tested on unseen sites

footer.legend: Evidence: ACTUAL = observed · DERIVED = calculated · ESTIMATED = modelled · PROXY = assumption · UNAVAILABLE = not in data. Two priority scales: MBP-P1…P4 (response) and BBS-P1…P4 (battery action); P1 = highest. Battery vs design is a separate scale from priority. Availability gaps in percentage points (pp).
gloss.bbt: BBT (Battery Backup Time): how long the battery keeps the site on air after PLN power goes off. Measured from the site's own outage events.
gloss.bbt_design: BBT Design: the backup time the battery should deliver (management standard 120 min). Problem criteria compare measured BBT against it.
gloss.censoring: Censoring: when PLN comes back before the battery runs out, we only know the battery lasted at least that long, not its full time.
gloss.dark_site: Dark site: a site with at least 2 months (of 6) in which power cuts took it off air for 8 hours or more. Thresholds are in Config.
gloss.derived_unverified: DERIVED-UNVERIFIED: a calculated BBT that the site's own downtime does not support. Check it on site before acting on it.
gloss.eta_gap: ETA gap: MBP travel time minus battery backup time. Positive means the site goes dark before the MBP arrives.
gloss.kaplan_meier: Kaplan-Meier: a statistical method that estimates battery life using both outages where the battery ran out and outages where PLN came back first.
gloss.pp: pp (percentage points): the plain difference between two percentages, e.g. 98.0% → 97.5% is −0.5 pp.
gloss.proxy: PROXY: a stand-in value used because the real data does not exist (e.g. a class default). Treat it as an assumption.
gloss.spearman: Spearman ρ: how strongly two things rise or fall together, from −1 to +1. Near 0 means no relation.

place.note.body: Reach = straight-line km ≤ {r} km radius and road ETA (km × {rf} road factor ÷ speed + {mob} min mobilisation) ≤ the site's BBT. New MBP locations are snapped to real MBP-P1/P2 sites (anchors), chosen greedily: each step adds the location that brings the most not-yet-reached MBP-P1/P2 sites within reach before BBT. Island sites (sea logistics) and sites whose battery is shorter than the mobilisation time (no MBP can ever arrive in time — battery action needed) are excluded from the denominator and shown separately. Dark hours avoided = battery-exhausted events (or dark months) × minutes the site would no longer be dark per event.

sim.note: Scenario-based allocation, not autonomous optimisation. Sites are served in priority order. For each site: (1) MBPs within the coverage radius, (2) hard constraint — keep only MBPs that arrive before the battery runs out, (3) among those prefer ETA, familiarity with the site, workload, (4) if none can arrive in time, fallback = earliest arrival and the site is flagged "late". One MBP serves one site per run. ETA is ESTIMATED (road factor × speed × traffic); MBP availability is PROXY — all available unless you mark them busy. Island sites have no road ETA and are reported separately.

trend.note: Clusters getting worse compares Q1 (Jan–Mar) with Q2 (Apr–Jun 2026). Primary signal: availability change (wall-clock, RAN) — ≤ −{tp} pp = Deteriorating, ≥ +{tp} pp = Improving. Secondary signal: change in the share of the cluster's sites that are dark (≥ {qm} of 3 months with ≥ {h} h power downtime), threshold ±{ts} pp of sites. When the two signals point in different directions (or availability is stable but the dark share moves) the cluster is Mixed, with the reason. Fewer than {min} sites with data in both quarters = Insufficient data. Thresholds are in Config.
